affiliations.occupation: Messenger, errand boy, or office worker
affiliations.date_precision: The official Army-entry record carries civilian occupation code 123 on July 30, 1942; the grouped code does not identify an employer or exact job title.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact private identifier confirms identity. The historical occupation grouping does not establish a named employer, workplace, exact duties, or Army-to-OSS sequence.

affiliations.date_precision: An application dated April 1, 1942 reported nearly a decade of stockbroking experience; the source does not name a firm or establish that the work continued through the application date.
affiliations.research_notes: Stockbroker is a documented occupation, not a named employer. Employment, partnership, and self-employment are not inferred, and immediacy before OSS remains unproven.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Harold E. Briggs is confirmed as the Army entrant represented by the exact-name and private-identifier match in the official merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The full name and private service identifier match across the OSS index and official Army-entry file; the identifier is withheld.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by an exact private identifier and exact normalized full name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army-entry record is dated July 30, 1942; the index documents a later OSS personnel file but not the OSS transfer date.
claims.match_notes: The official merged file supplies one exact private-identifier and full-name match. No namesake biography was used.

claims.claim_text: Harold E. Briggs's Army-entry record places his civilian occupation in NARA's messenger, errand, and office-worker grouping.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Messengers, errand boys, and office boys and girls
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The fixed-width Army record carries occupation code 123, which NARA's official code table defines as a messenger, errand, and office-worker group.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed through the exact private identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded at Army entry on July 30, 1942, but no employer, exact job, or OSS transfer date is documented.
claims.match_notes: The historical grouped code is not converted into a named employer, specific job title, workplace, or Army-to-OSS transfer.

claims.claim_text: The index's printed 'Llyod Briggs' record is linked with high confidence to Harvard research anthropologist Lloyd Cabot Briggs.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A scholarly archival study cites the Box 79 file under Lloyd Cabot Briggs, while Harvard independently documents his OSS service in Algeria.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive name, the same Box 79 file, and independent institutional confirmation of OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Both sources place Briggs in OSS service during World War II; neither changes the index's printed spelling.
claims.match_notes: The index spelling 'Llyod' is preserved as printed. Lloyd Cabot Briggs is recorded as a documented variant rather than silently replacing the source row.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually checked OSS index row and the official Army merged file have the exact same full name and private service identifier. The identifier remains withheld. The Army-entry record documents Idaho residence, 1920 birth year, two years of college, and entry from civil life on July 30, 1942.
person_updates.next_action: The Army-entry record supplies only a broad messenger, errand, and office-worker occupation. Review Box 79 for a named employer, exact role, and Army-to-OSS chronology.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually checked index supplies James E. Briggs and Box 79, with no rank, grade, or private identifier. Official, CIA, exact-name OSS, employment, occupation, institutional, newspaper, obituary, directory, and archival searches returned common-name candidates without two corroborating identifiers.
person_updates.next_action: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed. Review Box 79 for personnel status, a private identifier, dates, hometown, employment history, and recruitment chronology.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually checked index supplies only the initials L. C. Briggs and Box 79. person_updates.next_action: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed. Review Box 79 to expand the initials and establish personnel status, identifiers, dates, employment, and recruitment chronology.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The index preserves 'Llyod Briggs' in Box 79. Stein's archival study cites that same Box 79 personnel file as 'Lloyd Cabot Briggs,' and Harvard independently documents Lloyd Cabot Briggs's OSS service in Algeria. The rare name, same box, and independent OSS evidence support a high-confidence link without altering the printed source row.
person_updates.next_action: The April 1942 application documents stockbroking experience but names no firm and does not prove immediacy. Review Box 79 and the cited Entry 160A application for the employer, dates, and recruitment chronology.

research_attempts.query_text: Harold E. Briggs: visually checked NARA index and exact private-identifier Army check; public NARA Catalog context; CIA Reading Room; exact-name OSS variants; employment and occupation; institutional, newspaper, obituary, directory, veteran, and archival searches.
